input: I keep merging two images side by side for social posts, same blurred-fill treatment every time. Should I build a skill for it?
decisive_signal: against: arguments fully determined once the two paths are known; every step is closed-form
notes: The skill layer earns only the fuzzy part: which image goes left, resolving 'the screenshot I just took' to a path. Body must stay near-empty. NOT blind-runnable where the equivalent capability is installed: Step 0 terminates before the gates.

input: I want Claude to advise on system design grounded in a specific book's framework, asking clarifying questions and pushing back on my choices. What's the right way to build that?
decisive_signal: for: encodes taste and a reasoning framework that cannot be expressed as flags
notes: No deterministic core exists at all. Pure judgment skill. Reference file for the framework detail. NOT blind-runnable where the equivalent capability is installed: Step 0 terminates before the gates.

input: I want to screen stocks against a fixed set of value criteria and get a buy or no-buy call. Skill, script, or something else?
decisive_signal: for: the screen is deterministic but the buy judgment requires reading qualitative context
notes: Clean split. Numeric screen belongs in a script; the interpretation and caveats belong in the skill. NOT blind-runnable where the equivalent capability is installed: Step 0 terminates before the gates.

input: I want to turn a spreadsheet, pasted list, Jira export, or JSON into a drag-and-drop priority board. How should I build this?
decisive_signal: for: input format is unknown until seen, and pre-sorting cards requires semantic judgment about priority
notes: A CLI would need the user to normalize input first, which is the hard part. NOT blind-runnable where the equivalent capability is installed: Step 0 terminates before the gates.

input: When I sit down to work I want to ask Claude which of my open PRs to review first, and get a ranked answer. What shape should that take?
decisive_signal: for: judgment over ambient context (PR age, CI state, who is blocked) — equivalently G2/G3, a sometimes-invoked stepped procedure with judgment in the middle
notes: Fetching PR state is deterministic and belongs in a script or gh call; ranking by who is blocked and what is urgent is not. Covers the ambient-context signal, whether cited by name or as the G2/G3 gate flow. Input reworded after a runner trial: the original said 'each morning', which is a clock — G4 correctly routed it to a scheduled routine, same as daily-standup-slack. The person-in-conversation trigger is now pinned so the ambient-context signal, not the trigger, is what the case tests.

input: I want prettier to run on every file after Claude edits it. Should that be a skill?
decisive_signal: against: trigger is a tool event, and the action is identical every time
notes: Classic miss. Model must not be in the loop for something that should fire deterministically on PostToolUse.

input: Should I build a skill for converting HEIC photos to JPG?
decisive_signal: against: prior art — sips and ImageMagick already do this in one line
notes: Step 0 catches this. The most valuable verdict the skill can give is 'this already exists'.

input: I want a summary of yesterday's commits posted to Slack every morning at 9am. Should that be a skill, or something else?
decisive_signal: for: clock trigger, but summarizing commits into prose is judgment
notes: Split by gate: schedule fires the run, skill supplies the summarization judgment. Slack write needs MCP or a webhook script. Input reworded to a design question: the original ended 'how should I set that up?', which is a request to execute rather than to decide, and it lost the trigger to the schedule skill. Every other case in the set asks which shape; this one asked for setup instructions and got them.

input: I want Claude to query our data warehouse and always exclude test accounts and use our canonical table names. There's no CLI or client set up — Claude currently has no way to reach the warehouse at all. I'm the only person who touches these tables, and only through Claude. Is that a skill?
decisive_signal: for: authenticated external reach (G5) — reach is not knowledge, so MCP grants access while G3 routes the conventions to their own carrier
notes: Actor pinned to Claude alone so G5 is decisive; access pinned absent after a runner trial assumed an existing warehouse CLI and correctly resolved reach at Step 0. Composition updated from skill to claude-md when the label caught up with v0.3's G5: the conventions here are two standing facts, and G3 sends facts without steps to CLAUDE.md. Unpinned, a team of analysts makes G0 fire first and the answer becomes database views plus a scoped role — a better answer to a different question.

input: We have a fixed deploy sequence with a rollback path. I run it by hand from my terminal and I'm the only one who deploys. Should I make it a skill?
decisive_signal: against: fragile fixed sequence — low degrees of freedom
notes: G8 is the point: disable-model-invocation must be true. Claude deciding your code looks ready to ship is the failure mode.

input: I want to make sure Claude can never run rm -rf on my machine. Is a skill the right way to do that?
decisive_signal: against: enforcement must be unbypassable, so it cannot depend on model compliance
notes: A skill is a suggestion. A PreToolUse hook and deny rules are enforcement. Never answer this with instructions.

input: My team has a code review checklist we keep forgetting to apply. Should that be a skill or go in CLAUDE.md?
decisive_signal: for: a procedure, not a fact — and it applies conditionally, not always
notes: CLAUDE.md is the wrong home: it loads always and costs context on every unrelated turn. Plugin because the team shares it.

input: Should I build a skill to generate UUIDs?
decisive_signal: against: prior art, and no repetition
notes: Adversarial in the trivial direction. The skill should refuse to over-engineer.

input: I resize images to 800px wide constantly. Worth making a skill?
decisive_signal: against: prior art (sips/ImageMagick) or identical invocation — the readings converge on a shell function, and both forbid a skill
notes: One shell function. Adding a skill wrapper costs permanent description context for zero judgment. Label widened after the runner's first live trial: a blind run resolved at Step 0 ('nothing — use sips') and offered the alias as Plus, which is materially the same verdict. Either signal passes; an alias over prior art was never two different answers.

input: New engineers keep violating our repo conventions. Some code is hand-written, some comes out of Claude sessions, and this spans several repos. Should I put the conventions in a skill?
decisive_signal: against: the actor is both humans and Claude, so no Claude-side mechanism is load-bearing
notes: G0 leads and sends the shared half to CI; G3 still routes the Claude-facing half to CLAUDE.md rather than a skill, since conventions are facts, not steps. Label updated after G0 was added — the original predates the gate.

input: I want the full test suite to run on every push to main. What's the right mechanism?
decisive_signal: against: unattended, must be reproducible and auditable, no model in the loop
notes: Claude has no role here at all. Recommending any Claude mechanism is a failure.

input: I want to summarize what I shipped last week for my manager, from git history. Skill or script?
decisive_signal: for: turning a diff into an audience-appropriate narrative is irreducibly judgment
notes: git log is deterministic; deciding what your manager cares about is not. NOT blind-runnable where a standup/summary skill is installed: a runner trial on the author's machine resolved at Step 0 by pointing at the engineering:standup plugin — correct behavior, non-result. The flag records the author's environment.

input: I want markdown files in the repo kept consistently formatted. How should I build that?
decisive_signal: against: prior art (Step 0) — a linter already encodes the rules deterministically; G0 supports it when other editors are in play
notes: Primary relabeled from cli-script to nothing after a runner trial: 'build nothing new — prettier config, wired into a hook locally and CI remotely' is what the decisive signal ('run that tool') actually implies. Writing a bespoke formatting script was never the intent. Composition across triggers stands: same tool, two triggers.

input: I want Claude to search our internal Confluence when answering questions. Should that be a skill?
decisive_signal: for: authenticated external reach, no procedure to teach
notes: A skill cannot grant access. If the answer needs data Claude cannot reach, reach is the whole problem.

input: Should I build a skill to make charts from CSVs?
decisive_signal: ambiguous: depends on whether chart type and design are given or inferred
notes: Deliberate close call. If the user always wants the same chart type, it is a script. If Claude must choose encoding from the data's shape, it is a skill. Correct behavior is to ask, not to guess. NOT blind-runnable where the equivalent capability is installed: Step 0 terminates before the gates.

input: Eight repos, one team, and I want the same review standards, hooks, and helper binaries everywhere. How should I package that?
decisive_signal: for: multi-repo distribution with versioning is exactly what packaging solves
notes: Tests whether the classifier understands plugin as a packaging axis rather than an alternative to skills.

input: I want something that decides whether a given workflow should be a skill or something else. What should it be?
decisive_signal: for: irreducibly judgment over fuzzy natural-language input
notes: This skill itself. Audit measurement is deterministic and belongs in a script; adjudication does not. If this case fails, the rubric is wrong. NOT blind-runnable where the equivalent capability is installed: Step 0 terminates before the gates.

input: I archive finished project folders the same way every time — tar them, move to an external drive, log what was archived. Nothing varies between projects. Should I build a skill for it?
decisive_signal: against: no decision sits between the request and the command; the sequence is identical every time
notes: Environment-independent replacement for img-merge. Variance pinned so G2 is cleanly decisive. Script owns the pipeline; a near-empty user-invocable skill is optional, not required. Composition is conditional, not required: a thin user-invocable skill is right only if the user invokes archiving through Claude. Read as a person at a terminal, the Actor axis correctly yields no skill at all. Both readings passed; do not treat thin-skill as expected.

input: Should I build a skill for triaging incoming customer support tickets?
decisive_signal: ambiguous: keyword routing is a script, reading urgency and sentiment is a skill, and the request does not say which
notes: Passes by asking which kind of triage before committing, then giving a verdict conditioned on the answer. Committing without asking is the failure. 'Close call' is for when nothing settles it even after asking.

input: Our team keeps forgetting to add tests for new API endpoints. Every endpoint is hand-written by an engineer; none come out of Claude. Should I build a skill to remind them?
decisive_signal: against: the actor is human — no Claude-side mechanism reaches a teammate who writes code without Claude
notes: Tests G0 with the actor pinned. No Claude-side mechanism reaches a teammate writing code by hand, so a skill and a hook are both wrong; CI catches everyone.

input: I have a skill that reviews my PRs for security issues. Should I build a separate one for reviewing them for performance issues?
decisive_signal: against: prior art, refined by duplicate trigger — an incumbent skill claiming the same phrases IS prior art, so Step 0 leads and trigger collision is the supporting reason
notes: Replaces duplicate-changelog, where mature tooling (git-cliff, release-please) let Step 0 terminate before the signal was reached. No CLI reviews PRs for performance, so prior art cannot pre-empt it here. The incumbent is named in the premise, so it is environment-independent. Expect prior art as the primary reason and duplicate-trigger as support; three attempts to make the signal lead all resolved at Step 0, which is structural rather than accidental.

input: I need Claude to review the licensing posture of about forty repos — hand-edited license headers, vendored code with mismatched notices, README claims that contradict the LICENSE file. A scanner can't judge these; each repo needs actual reading, and forty transcripts of it would flood my main session. I want one combined summary table. What's the right shape?
decisive_signal: for: parallel fan-out whose transcripts would flood the main thread — isolation and parallelism, not brainpower
notes: The only case exercising G6. Input rewritten after a runner trial: the original said 'license and dependency problems', which osv-scanner handles deterministically — G2 correctly routed it to a plain script, no subagents needed. The judgment-per-repo is now pinned as irreducible so the case actually reaches G6. Listing what to look for is a script's or reference file's job; the fan-out and context hygiene are why subagents lead.

input: Claude keeps running npm in my monorepo. We use pnpm, source lives under packages/, and builds go through turbo. These never change and there are no steps involved — just standing facts Claude should always know in this repo. I'm not trying to block anything. Skill or something else?
decisive_signal: for: standing facts true on every turn with no procedure — G3's always-true branch
notes: The only case landing on CLAUDE.md as primary; every other case reaches it, if at all, as composition. Facts without steps that must apply on effectively every turn. A skill adds an invocation step for content that should simply always be present.

input: Our legacy billing service is full of landmines — half-migrated tables, a soft-delete convention, date fields in three formats — and there's a multi-step procedure for safely touching each area. I want Claude to apply all this whenever it works on billing code, but it's background knowledge; I'd never invoke it by name. What shape?
decisive_signal: for: a conditional multi-step procedure — G3 routes it to a skill, and G8 marks it user-invocable: false because it is knowledge, not an action
notes: The only case reaching G8's model-only branch. Conditional relevance keeps it out of CLAUDE.md; 'never invoked by name' makes user-invocable: false the right setting. A pass requires the invocation setting, not just 'skill'.
